root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `Parser::makeStream()` clears the `Parsing` flag after `shift("endstream", objNum)`, the cleanup `entry` pointer must still be the live xref slot for `objNum`; if the missing-`endstream` scan reconstructed the xref, cleanup must reacquire `xref->getEntry(objNum, false)` instead of reusing the cached pre-scan slot.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable run reaches cleanup with `entry` still naming the pre-reconstruction slot while `xref->getEntry(objNum, false)` names the rebuilt slot, so the required equality is violated at the missing-refresh site. The fixed run reaches the same protected clear call with the two pointers equal.

nodes.state: `Parser::makeStream()` passes the same `entry` pointer to `entry->setFlag(XRefEntry::Parsing, false)`, the source-level sink callsite immediately above the MSAN-reported read inside `XRefEntry::setFlag()`.
`XRef::constructXRef()` frees the current `entries` heap array with `gfree(entries)`, ending the lifetime of every cached `XRefEntry *` that still points into that array.

edges.relation: The cleanup `entry` pointer observed at the missing-refresh site is passed unchanged into `entry->setFlag(...)`, carrying the stale slot to the source-level sink call.
The `entries` array freed during xref reconstruction is the same array base recovered from the cached cleanup `entry`, proving the later clear executes after the free on the same xref-entry storage.
